name: Jamin
overview: Jamin is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, identified as the son of Ram and grandson of Jerahmeel. His mention in Scripture is brief, primarily noting his genealogical position within the tribe of Judah as recorded in 1 Chronicles 2:27. There are no additional notes or detailed narratives about his life or actions.
namesAndTitles: The name Jamin likely means 'right hand' or 'south,' which may symbolize strength or good fortune. This proper name is not indicated to have been given directly by God but reflects a meaningful Hebrew term as noted in 1 Chronicles 2:27.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jamin as the son of Ram, who is in turn the son of Jerahmeel, establishing Jamin’s place within a specific family line in the tribe of Judah. No other family relationships are documented beyond this lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Jamin's significance lies in his role within the genealogical record of Judah, demonstrating the continuation of the tribe’s lineage. His mention helps trace the ancestry of key biblical figures and reflects the importance of preserving family lines in the Old Testament narrative. While not a prominent character in terms of narrative actions, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of God in maintaining His covenant through the descendants of Judah.
